title: Do / did / done
subtitle: What do you do? do the washing
summary: Use do in questions and negatives, ask about people's jobs with What do you do?, and learn the jobs we do at home.

lesson.heading: Do as a helping verb
lesson.text: We use **do**, **does** and **did** to make questions, short answers and negatives with other verbs.

examples.text: **Do** you like tennis? **Did** they like the film?
*A:* Do you like tennis? *B:* Yes, I **do**.
*A:* Did they like the film? *B:* Yes, they **did**.
He **doesn't** play well. Leo **didn't** see it.
I love football. So **does** Matteo. So **did** I.

lesson.heading: Do as a general verb
lesson.text: **Do** is also a normal verb. We use it to ask what is happening now, and to talk about doing nothing at all.

examples.text: On Saturdays I usually **do** nothing. I just relax.

lesson.heading: What do you do?
lesson.text: **What do you do?** means *What is your job?* It is one of the first questions people ask a new friend.

examples.text: *A:* What **do** you **do**? *B:* I'm a student. / I'm a hairdresser.
*A:* What **does** your wife **do**? *B:* She's a doctor. / She's a teacher.

lesson.heading: do + activity
rows: wash the plates and cups after a meal
do the work your teacher gives you
move your body to keep fit
buy and sell with a company
try as hard as you can

lesson.heading: Using the do expressions
lesson.text: Learn these expressions as whole phrases. Note that we say **do the washing** for clothes and **do the washing-up** for plates and cups.

examples.text: *A:* Did you **do the washing** this morning? *B:* No, I'm going to **do** it later.
Our company **does a lot of business with** the US.
The homework is very difficult - just **do your best**.
The man in the kitchen is **doing the washing-up**.

lesson.text: Make a note of every expression with do that you meet when you read in English - there are a lot of them.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What ___ your wife do? *B:* She's a doctor.
exercises.explanation: What does he / she do? asks about a person's job.

exercises.prompt: On Saturdays I usually do ___. I just relax at home.
exercises.explanation: Do nothing means have a rest and not work.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you like tennis? *B:* Yes, I ___.
exercises.explanation: The short answer uses the same helping verb as the question.

exercises.statement: Where did you went on your holidays?
exercises.explanation: Where did you go on your holidays? After did we use the simple form of the verb.

exercises.statement: No, we don't go to Wales this year. We went to Scotland.
exercises.explanation: No, we didn't go to Wales this year. We went to Scotland.

exercises.statement: Do your grandmother lives in Scotland?
exercises.explanation: Does your grandmother live in Scotland?

exercises.prompt: *A:* Does your grandmother live in Scotland? *B:* No, she doesn't, but my uncle ___.
exercises.explanation: In a short answer we repeat the helping verb: he does, she doesn't.

exercises.prompt: Match each job at home with the right expression with do.

pairs.left: the plates and cups after a meal
the cleaning and tidying at home
the work your teacher gives you

exercises.prompt: Our company ___ a lot of business with the US.
exercises.explanation: We do business with a company or a country.

exercises.prompt: The homework is very difficult - just do your ___.
exercises.explanation: Do your best means try as hard as you can.

exercises.prompt: The man in the garden is planting flowers. What is he doing?
exercises.explanation: We do the gardening when we look after the garden.

exercises.prompt: Is each sentence about the present or about the past?
Ask a new friend what their wife's job is.
exercises.explanation: What do / does ... do? asks about a job.
